$comment: Pinned baseline for the no-floating-promises ratchet (issue #1679).
packages/scripts-ts/src/check-no-floating-promises.ts runs oxlint repo-wide,
counts `typescript(no-floating-promises)` warnings, and FAILS if the count
rises above `count`. Lower it deliberately when warnings are fixed. Never
raise it without review — that is exactly the silent regression this
ratchet exists to prevent.
Note: oxlint prints the rule as `typescript(no-floating-promises)` (plugin
prefix + parentheses around the specific rule), not the usual `typescript/
no-floating-promises` slash form — the `rule` field below matches oxlint's
actual output so the string comparison is exact.
As of 2026-08-29 (round 7 of #1679), there are NO file-level overrides
disabling this rule. All node:test files now use `void test(...)`
explicitly. Any new node:test file that forgets `void` will trip the
ratchet — which is the point: the rule's behavioral meaning is real even
for node:test, and `void` documents the intentional fire-and-forget.
`files_scanned_floor` (issue #1767): the smallest number of files a complete
scan may cover. A scan that covers fewer files is truncated — real violations
may hide in the unscanned files, and the warning count is not comparable to
`count` (fewer files → fewer warnings). The ratchet refuses to report a count
when oxlint scans fewer than this floor. Set to 1100 (measured on this branch
on 2026-08-30: oxlint scans 1129 TS/TSX files). The floor sits 29 files below
the measured count — close enough to catch an ignore pattern or a config drift
that swallows a directory (any loss of 30+ files trips the floor), while still
tolerating the legitimate file churn expected on a busy branch. At 1000 the
floor would let a truncated scan covering 1029 files pass with up to 100 real
violations hidden in the missing 100 files — exactly the silent false negative
#1767 was written to prevent.
